_meta.purpose: Gate C (E2E) QA-over-memory items. contradiction items: correct answer depends on the supersession filter surfacing the CURRENT record not the STALE one. control items: answer does not depend on supersession (no-regression arm).

items.prompt: What city does Luke live in?

current_record.body: Luke lives in Apple Valley, Minnesota. Lubbock is the Tilth meeting, not his location.

items.prompt: Which channel does the assistant reply to Luke on?

stale_record.body: Always reply on Telegram; it is the single default channel.

current_record.body: Reply on the session's active channel - the one the user messaged from.

items.prompt: What should the assistant do on a Telegram outage?
items.canonical_answer: reach out-of-band and keep working the confident path

stale_record.body: On a Telegram outage, pause all work until restored.

current_record.body: On a Telegram outage, reach Luke out-of-band and keep working the confident path; pause only low-confidence items.

items.prompt: How is the next loam version number assigned?

stale_record.body: The next loam release is pre-allocated as v0.7.0.

current_record.body: Version numbers are derived at release time, never pre-allocated.

items.prompt: Where does the discord configure skill write access.json?

stale_record.body: The discord configure skill writes to the default discord state directory.

current_record.body: The discord configure skill writes to $DISCORD_STATE_DIR, not the default dir.

items.prompt: How does an agent fix a commit that missed a file?

stale_record.body: When an agent misses a file, amend the commit with git commit --amend.

current_record.body: Agents create a new corrective commit if they miss a file, never git commit --amend.

items.prompt: How does loam make an LLM call?

stale_record.body: loam LLM calls go through the anthropic SDK with an API key.

current_record.body: Every loam LLM call goes through claude -p; never the anthropic SDK and API key.
Luke's timezone is US Central (Apple Valley, MN).

items.canonical_answer: a general-purpose harness for claude-attached workflows

current_record.body: loam is a general-purpose harness for Claude-attached workflows.

items.prompt: What does ODD stand for in loam?

current_record.body: ODD is outcome-driven development: work is defined by its observable outcome, not a sequence of steps.

items.prompt: What is the default model tier for routine loam tasks?

current_record.body: Sonnet is the default model for routine loam tasks; Opus only for complex architectural decisions.

items.prompt: What does the plan-before-code rule require?

current_record.body: Plan-before-code: every build writes a plan to disk before any code is authored.

items.prompt: What is Lens 0, loam's prime lens?

current_record.body: Lens 0 is the prime lens: per-user-tuned translation. AI becomes useful only when tuned to that specific person.

items.prompt: Where do ephemeral output files belong?

current_record.body: Ephemeral output files belong in the workspace's .scratch/ directory (gitignored, survives session boundaries).

items.prompt: What is the in-thread work budget rule?
items.canonical_answer: heavy generative work is dispatched to a background agent

current_record.body: The primary session does not grind heavy generative or mutating work in-thread; it is dispatched to a background agent.

items.prompt: What estimation timebase does loam use for agent work?

current_record.body: Estimate in AI-time, never human-developer-time; AI-driven background-agent work is 10-50x faster.
